title: Telemetry ingest with rates, file paths, a boundary line and a schema
persona: A platform engineer explaining the telemetry ingest path to an agent before asking where events get dropped under load; they think in rates and know roughly which repo file each box is.
topic: where telemetry events get dropped under load
realism: Capacity conversations put numbers on arrows ('~50k/s'), file paths beside boxes so people can go look, a line separating the customer's process from our cluster, and the event's fields written out; on a whiteboard all of that is just writing placed next to the thing it describes.

steps.say: This is the ingest path, and I'll put numbers on it.
Events start in the SDK inside the customer's app.
Everything right of this line is ours.
Peak is about fifty thousand events a second coming into the collector.
The collector lives in cmd collector server dot go.
It batches five hundred at a time into the events raw topic.
Twenty four partitions, I'm fairly sure.
The enricher reads it, that's the python service, and this one is the bottleneck.
I think it does maybe eight thousand a second per pod and we run four, which doesn't add up to fifty.
Then it lands in ClickHouse, and end to end we promise under two seconds at p ninety nine.
And here's what an event looks like.
Timestamp, tenant, a name, and a bag of properties.
My guess is we drop when the enricher lags past the topic's retention.

steps.note: retention on events.raw is 6h I believe

steps.say: So check the numbers, and whether the collector itself sheds load before Kafka.

story: the dashed vertical line separates the customer's app (left: SDK) from their own cluster (right: Collector, events.raw, Enricher, ClickHouse)
'~50k events/s' is the peak rate on the SDK → Collector arrow
the Collector is in cmd/collector/server.go and the Enricher in services/enricher/main.py
events.raw is a Kafka topic with 24 partitions (they are fairly sure), fed in batches of 500
'~8k/s/pod, 4 pods?' is about the Enricher, and they point out 4 × 8k/s is well under 50k/s: they think the Enricher is the bottleneck
'p99 < 2s' is their end-to-end latency promise, near the Enricher → ClickHouse arrow
the Event schema has four fields, one per line: ts int64, tenant_id string, name string, props map<string,any>
their guess is that events are dropped when the Enricher lags past events.raw's retention (they believe 6 h), and they want to know whether the Collector sheds load before Kafka
partner_should_ask_about: what the Collector does when Kafka is slow or full
how many Enricher pods actually run
